text:
maria (support): Hey team — escalated from Acme Mobile. They see SSE sessions delivering a first small chunk, then 30–40s of silence, then client reconnects and gets only the last partial event. Happening for ~20% of mobile users behind various carrier NATs. Customer expecting a streaming transcript.

jamie (sre): Are we seeing 499s / broken pipes in front-door logs or app errors? Any pattern for ALB vs Cloudflare?

maria (support): ALB in front of our k8s ingress for this customer; some requests originate via Cloudflare spectrum in other regions. App logs show a few broken pipe errors and a couple 524/524-like timeouts from Cloudflare. Example app log: `2026-02-17T14:02:11Z write failed: write tcp 10.4.2.12:443->10.5.1.99:51234: use of closed network connection`

lee (eng-runtime): That looks like upstream connection half-close/idle. Do we have any evidence of proxy injecting TCP RST after an idle probe? Envoy/ALB health/idle timeouts mismatch often surface like this.

arjun (eng-infra): Quick config notes: ALB idle timeout default = 60s, nginx ingress-proxy proxy_read_timeout typically 60s, Cloudflare default idle timeout for Spectrum/Argo clients can be ~100s but CDN may terminate on long silence. But carriers drop idle TCP after ~30s in some mobile networks.

maria (support): Customer says silence starts ~32s after last chunk. They run a simple repro with curl on mobile emulator that mirrors report. Repro they used: 

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.acme.example/v1/stream?model=small" \
  --max-time 300
```

They see one `data: {partial}` chunk then nothing, then client reconnects.

jamie (sre): Can you paste a degraded request trace (X-Request-ID) so I can check ALB logs and ingress pod for keepalive/close events? Also, does the app emit partial-flush chunks with a trailing newline? Some proxies will coalesce until a flush boundary.

maria (support): Provided trace id: rid=acme-20260217-7f3a. ALB logs show `target: 10.4.2.12:443 code: 504` around same period for one instance, and a bunch of `Client: 10.5.1.99: aborted` for others.

lee (eng-runtime): Two likely interacting things: (1) upstream or client NAT drops idle TCP after ~30s, (2) intermediate proxy or CDN is buffering and not passing small flushes through. If we emit very small heartbeat bytes more frequently (<15s) it usually keeps carriers alive. Also make sure Transfer-Encoding: chunked is used and response doesn't set Content-Length.

arjun (eng-infra): On nginx/ingress we have proxy_buffering on by default for some locations — that will buffer chunks until buffer full or request end. For Envoy-based ingress we need `proxy_buffering off` (nginx) or set `flush_interval` for envoy filter. Cloudflare also has Stream/HTTP buffering behaviors depending on Worker/Argo settings.

maria (support): Customer asked for a workaround they can apply without infra changes. Any options?

lee (eng-runtime): App-level workarounds (fastest): send a lightweight SSE comment/heartbeat every 10s (e.g. `: heartbeat\n\n`) or send a 1-byte data chunk `data: \n\n` to force flush. Also ensure server explicitly calls the runtime flush APIs (we use response.flush()). Example pseudo: 

```
// every 10s
w.Write([]byte(": hb\\n\\n"))
w.(http.Flusher).Flush()
```

This keeps carrier NAT/ALB from idling and bypasses proxy coalescing if not buffered.

jamie (sre): For infra side, we can try: set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; tcp_nodelay on;` on nginx ingress location for SSE routes. For Envoy we can set `max_response_bytes_to_buffer` low and enable `stream_idle_timeout` or `connection_idle_timeout` adjustments. I'll draft the change. :memo:

arjun (eng-infra): I'll also check ALB idle timeout — increasing to 120s for this customer’s TG could reduce false closes. But note mobile carriers will still kill flows; client heartbeats are more robust.

maria (support): Customer OK with app heartbeat change, wants docs for recommended headers and sample code. Also asked if this has billing implications (reconnects causing duplicate partial transcripts).

lee (eng-runtime): Docs: recommend SSE routes set `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, no `Content-Length`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, `Connection: keep-alive`. Send comment heartbeats every 10s and include an `event: retry` policy if needed. Billing: yes, reconnects may replay tokens/requests; advise idempotency token on resume if transcript pieces are re-requested, or server-side session resume to avoid double-charging.

maria (support): Great. I'll send the sample snippets and the suggested nginx/Envoy config. Customer will implement heartbeat first. I'll follow up with logs after they roll. Thanks all. :pray:

cloudflare-bot: Note — Cloudflare may rewrite certain chunk boundaries when Workers are present; if customer has Worker or managed rules, disable buffering there or enable `workers.dev` streaming with streaming responses to preserve chunk boundaries.
